title: Citing Organizations as authors
description:
Dear Posit people,

first of all. Thank you for providing RStudio!

When I try to cite a source with an organization as author from Zotero, using the visual markdon/quarto editor, the words get mixed up e.g. "World Health Organization" will end up as "Organization, World Health".

Usually Zotero would put single field authors in dubble braces "{{World Health Organization}}" in the bibtex export to keep the correct order of the words. But this does not happen, when the citation is entered into references.bib by the citing function of RStudios visual editor.

I am not entirely sure, but it seems to be a problem of RStudio, not of Zotero or Pandoc.

Could you please check this?

Thank you very much in advance and kind regards
Johann Popp

title: visual inserts text that breaks kramdown-rfc formatted file
description:
For a variety of reasons I am trying to use RStudio visual markdown to compose an Internet Draft style documents formatted In kramdown-rfc style ( see https://github.com/cabo/kramdown-rfc )

My current problem is that when I enter visual mode to edit my markdown doc the file is modified so that kramdown-rfc tools no longer work with the file that worked previously. I have narrowed the problem down to the following 2 changes that visual makes to the file. 
(1) it escapes the hashtag in the IDL for the ascii-art diagram I have included in a code block and 
(2) it inserts a blank line between the code block and the IDL

These 2 things break kramdown-rfc apps from seeing it as valid kramdown-rfc markdown

I am wondering if there are configuration options that might be added to the yaml preface to prevent these 2 modifications from being made? Or perhaps some other approach?

The initial file, before entering visual mode is shown below...

title: package citations
description:
Where does the visual editor pull citations from? They are different from that provided by citation("*package name*"). For example, compare the entry for the tidyverse package as created by the visual editor:

@article{tidyverse,
	title = {Welcome to the {\textbraceleft}tidyverse{\textbraceright}},
	author = {Wickham, Hadley and Averick, Mara and Bryan, Jennifer and Chang, Winston and McGowan, {Lucy D'Agostino} and {François}, Romain and Grolemund, Garrett and Hayes, Alex and Henry, Lionel and Hester, Jim and Kuhn, Max and Pedersen, Thomas Lin and Miller, Evan and Bache, Stephan Milton and {Müller}, Kirill and Ooms, Jeroen and Robinson, David and Seidel, Dana Paige and Spinu, Vitalie and Takahashi, Kohske and Vaughan, Davis and Wilke, Claus and Woo, Kara and Yutani, Hiroaki},
	year = {2019},
	date = {2019},
	pages = {1686},
	volume = {4},
	doi = {10.21105/joss.01686}
}

versus what is produced by citation("tidyverse"),

@Article{,
    title = {Welcome to the {tidyverse}},
    author = {Hadley Wickham and Mara Averick and Jennifer Bryan and Winston Chang and Lucy D'Agostino McGowan and Romain François and Garrett Grolemund and Alex Hayes and Lionel Henry and Jim Hester and Max Kuhn and Thomas Lin Pedersen and Evan Miller and Stephan Milton Bache and Kirill Müller and Jeroen Ooms and David Robinson and Dana Paige Seidel and Vitalie Spinu and Kohske Takahashi and Davis Vaughan and Claus Wilke and Kara Woo and Hiroaki Yutani},
    year = {2019},
    journal = {Journal of Open Source Software},
    volume = {4},
    number = {43},
    pages = {1686},
    doi = {10.21105/joss.01686},
  }

Note that the visual editor version has errors in formatting and has dropped the journal name. I have found that almost every entry needs to be edited.

title: Visual breaks figure path generated by code placed inside `![](...)` replacing `` (accent) and space by URL-encode %60 and %20
description:
When writing a document I often switch between "source" and "visual" editor. Sometimes switching to "visual" edit the source code. In the case presented here, the edit breaks a figure inserted using the structure ```![](`r knitr::fig_chunk()`)```.

Please if this is not a bug let me know how to avoid it.

# Here is a reproducible example:

## Starting point:

````
---
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# library(ragg) # in the screenshot but not needed and does not change the output
library(ggplot2)
```

## Display and save

```{r display, dev='png', fig.show='hide'}
p <- ggplot(mtcars) + 
  geom_point(aes(mpg, disp, colour = hp))
p
```
![mtcars plot](`r knitr::fig_chunk('display','png')`)

````

## Click on "Visual" and than go back to "Source"

````
---
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}

# library(ragg)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Display and save

```{r display, dev='png', fig.show='hide'}

  geom_point(aes(mpg, disp, colour = hp))
p
```

![mtcars plot](%60r%20knitr::fig_chunk('display','png')%60)
````

title: more wrapping option
description:
hello,

line wrapping does help a lot for text review. It would be nice to be able to wrap with multiple options

at sentences (`wrap: sentence`)
at a specific length (similar to `wrap: 80`)
( an additional option for wrapping at commas in the last 15 available characters would also be cool)

this does unfortunately not work:

```
editor_options:
  markdown:
    wrap:
      - sentence
      - 80
```

title: Lack of an option to hide code chunks
description: Hi, this feature looks really great. One thing I have noticed though is that in the classic RMarkdown editor one can hide code chunks while working on the .Rmd itself (by clicking the arrow on the left, or with shortcuts as Alt+O). However, in the Visual Editor this option is not possible. I find this a bit umcomfortable in order to navigate the document, especially when there are large code chunks in the middle of large text sections. If you only want to focus on the text, having to scroll down an up the code many times may not be the best solution. Would it be possible to add the feature to hide code chunks to the visual editor too? Thanks a lot!

title: Difficulty (minor) inserting multiple citations
description:
Hi, I am really enjoying this new feature. I have a minor issue to raise when attempting to insert multiple citations: if I select multiple citations with the '+' sign then these appear in the 'selected citation keys' box (as expected), however if I start typing in the 'Search for citation' box then all my currently selected citations disappear from the 'selected citation keys' box. 

Would it be possible to allow the user to use the 'search for citation' box without clearing any citations that have already been selected? Thanks
